entries.title: The Barrens
body: A vast, dry savannah in the heart of Kalimdor, stretching from the edge of Ashenvale in the north to the cliffs of Thousand Needles in the south, and from the mountains of Stonetalon to the sea. Long grass, thorn trees and baked red earth cover most of it, and zhevra, kodo, lions and raptors roam the plains.

Long ago the land was green, until war and upheaval scorched it. Yet in the past few years new oases have appeared, and the druids sense a strange power seeping up from below that changes the plants and beasts that drink from them.

The Horde holds the roads. Its fortress at the Crossroads links Durotar, Mulgore and Ashenvale, and goblins run the free port of Ratchet on the coast. Everything else is contested: quilboars, centaurs and harpies raid the caravans, goblin prospectors and dwarven diggers tear at the earth, and soldiers of Theramore hold a fort on the southern shore.
sources: quest 870 description (the Barrens once lush, new oases, power leaking)
quests 894, 843, 891 (Venture Company, Bael Modan dwarves, Northwatch Hold)
pre-Cataclysm lore: geography of the Barrens

entries.title: The Crossroads
body: A walled Horde town where the roads of the northern Barrens meet: east to Durotar, west to Stonetalon, north to Ashenvale and south towards Camp Taurajo and Ratchet. Orcs and tauren live side by side here, and it has become the meeting place of both peoples in the Barrens.

Thork commands its defences in the Warchief's name. Wind riders carry travellers to Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff, the inn and the merchants do lively business with the hunters who pass through, and supplies come in by caravan from Durotar when the quilboars let them through.

It is a busy, slightly harried place. Even the guards' wages are not safe: a shipment of payroll silver was carried off from the watch tower by raptors, which nobody believed until one of the thieves was caught.
sources: creature 3433 Tatternack Steelforge gossip (hub of orc and tauren cultures)

entries.title: Far Watch Post
body: A Horde watch post on the Barrens side of the Southfury River, guarding the road that crosses over from Durotar. It is the first stop for orcs and trolls heading west into the savannah.

Kargal Battlescar runs it with the help of his scout, Takrin Pathseeker, and signs up every capable recruit for duty in the Barrens before sending them on to the Crossroads. The shaman Ak'Zeloth works nearby on behalf of Neeru Fireblade of Orgrimmar, keeping an eye on the demonic cult that has a foothold in the hills to the north-west.
sources: quest 809 description (Far Watch Post on the border, Ak'Zeloth, Neeru's assistant)

entries.title: Dreadmist Peak
body: A steep hill in the northern Barrens, its summit wrapped in a cave where the Burning Blade keeps an altar of fire. Above the altar rested the Demon Seed, the object of demonic power around which the cult gathers, and acolytes and bruisers of the cult guard the slopes.

Neeru Fireblade sent word that the Seed must be destroyed, and his assistant Ak'Zeloth prepared power stones to break its link with the Burning Legion. Ak'Zeloth found it strange that Neeru wanted the Seed gone. When it shattered, the blast rippled out through the ether, and he warned that whoever had been using it would want to know why.
sources: creatures 3379 Burning Blade Bruiser, 3380 Burning Blade Acolyte

entries.title: The Forgotten Pools
body: A cluster of pools north-west of the Crossroads, one of the new oases that have sprung up in the Barrens in recent years. At the bottom of its waters is a fissure in the earth, with gas bubbling up from below: the first clue the druids found to the source of the oases' power.
The Kolkar centaurs camp nearby. Barak Kodobane, one of the new leaders who rallied the Kolkar into a real threat, made his camp beside the pools.

entries.title: The Stagnant Oasis
body: A murky oasis south-east of the Crossroads. Like the Forgotten Pools it hides a bubbling fissure, and dead seeds placed inside it sprouted into life, proof that whatever lies beneath can make life out of nothing.
The Kolkar have their command tent here, and the dervish Verog roams out from it across the plains. South-west of the oasis are the nests of the scytheclaw raptors.
sources: quest 905 description (scytheclaw nests south-west of the Stagnant Oasis)

entries.title: Lushwater Oasis
body: The largest and greenest of the oases, south of the Crossroads. Snapjaw turtles swim in its waters, and their shells have taken on an inner glow and a taint that the druids had never seen before.
Hezrul Bloodmark, warlord of all the Kolkar in the Barrens, leads his people from here. The Horde believes that without him the Kolkar would split apart.

entries.title: The Wailing Caverns
body: A cave system beneath the Barrens, entered through a mound in the hills near Lushwater Oasis. The night elf druid Naralex went down into it with his disciples, meaning to enter the Emerald Dream and grow the Barrens back into a forest.

His dream turned into a nightmare. Strange deviate beasts crawled up from below, and some of his followers, the Druids of the Fang, have gone over to the nightmare and want to remake the Barrens in its image. The remaining Disciples of Naralex camp at the entrance, some hoping to wake their master and others simply trying to clear the caves of the creatures his dreaming has spawned.
sources: quest 1489 description (the Wailing Caverns as source of the taint)

entries.title: Ratchet
body: A goblin port on the eastern coast, the main harbour of the Barrens. Ships sail from its docks to Booty Bay, and like other goblin towns it trades with anyone who pays and keeps the peace with hired bruisers.

Gazlowe runs the town. Wharfmaster Dizzywig keeps the shipping ledgers, the Tinkers' Union tests its shredders here under Sputtervalve, and every other goblin on the docks has a scheme going, from smart drinks brewed out of raptor horn to spider-egg omelettes for the Booty Bay market.

entries.title: The Merchant Coast
body: The sandy shore that runs south from Ratchet towards Northwatch Hold. Just south of the town the Southsea Freebooters have set up a pirate camp, and they raid the trading ships coming in and out of the harbour.

Their best-known captain is Baron Longshore of Gilneas, master of a ship called the Heedless, with a price on his head for piracy. Gazlowe blames the trade fleets of Undermine for letting the pirates run loose, and has lost goods meant for his observatory to them.
sources: quest 891 (south along the Merchant Coast to the Hold)

entries.title: Northwatch Hold
body: A fortress of Theramore on the southern coast of the Barrens, with cannons trained on the sea. Its soldiers are nervous and quick to shoot, and under Captain Fairmount they have sunk ship after ship, among them the privateers of Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun out of Ratchet.

The garrison treats any vessel as an enemy. When a moonshine runner went down off the coast, its only survivor, a deckhand named Gilthares Firebough, was locked in the Hold as a threat to the Alliance.
sources: quest 874 (the coast is held by humans)

entries.title: Camp Taurajo
body: A tauren camp in the southern Barrens, on the road towards Thousand Needles. Its people share the Horde's war against the quilboars of the south, and its hunters, led by Jorn Skyseer, follow the great beasts of the plains.

Two of its residents are not tauren. Tatternack Steelforge, an orc smith, was sent by the Warchief to study the weapons of every people in the Barrens, even quilboar and centaur. And in a cage at the edge of camp sits Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar prisoner with a grudge against his own kind.

entries.title: Bael Modan
body: A dwarven excavation in the southern Barrens, blasted into land that was once the birthplace of a tauren tribe. The dwarves' explosives and machines tear open the hills, and a keep built to defend the dig is now strong enough to strike out from it. Prospector Khazgorm ran the digging and General Twinbraid commands the keep, where a great flying machine is the site's pride.

The dig's first great find was a gem called the Tear of the Moons. Twinbraid called it cursed and locked it in the keep, driving off the one who first claimed it, an exile named Feegly who still raves about getting it back. The tauren Gann Stonespire walks the nearby roads alone, determined to reclaim his people's land.
sources: quests 843, 846, 849 descriptions, progress and offer texts

entries.title: The Sludge Fen
body: An oily marsh in the northern Barrens where the Venture Company drills for oil, with derricks, shredders and a small research site full of experimental machinery. Nearby the company also works the Boulder Lode Mine, where one miner dug up an emerald the size of a fist.

Goblins of the rival Tinkers' Union watch the site closely. One of their pilots slipped into a Venture shredder and drove it out, and a strange device called the samophlange was taken from the research console. Boss Copperplug of the mine holds the device's manual and hands out its secrets only to a trusted few.

entries.title: Field of Giants
body: A stretch of the southern Barrens dotted with the earthen mounds of insect-like creatures, the silithid. Nobody in the Horde knows much about them, but they seem cleverer than any normal beast and swarm anyone who disturbs their eggs.

The troll Korran watches them from the Crossroads for his masters in Orgrimmar, and the more travellers tell him, the more worried he becomes. A huge silithid known as the Harvester roams the field, and even the hunter Jorn Skyseer believes such creatures do not belong in the Barrens and may herald a grim future.
sources: creatures 3250-3253 Silithid Creeper, Grub, Swarmer, Harvester

entries.title: The Dry Hills
body: Rough, dusty hills in the north-western Barrens where the Witchwing harpies have their nests. They raid the Horde's caravans relentlessly, and their flocks are organised in ranks of slayers, ambushers and windcallers beneath a single leader.

The harpies are not native to the Barrens; they came from the Stonetalon Mountains. Their leader, Serena Bloodfeather, wages her war on the Horde for a personal reason: revenge for her sister, killed years ago by Rexxar.

entries.title: Raptor Grounds
body: A large field of raptor nests south of Ratchet. The raptors of the Barrens are cleverer than raptors elsewhere: they raided the Crossroads watch tower, carried off a chest of silver and hid it among their nests.
Nobody can say what a raptor wants with silver. The goblins of Ratchet are convinced the cleverness lives in their horns, and have tried to grind them into drinks.

entries.title: Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs
body: Two vast warrens of thorn at the southern edge of the Barrens, the holiest places of the quilboars. They believe the thorns grew from the body of their fallen god Agamaggan; the Kraul is his resting place, and the entrance to the Downs is his great maw.

Both have turned dark. A crone named Charlga Razorflank musters an army in the Kraul, and the raiders who torment the Crossroads came out of it. In the Downs the quilboars have struck a bargain with the Scourge, and the dead walk among them.
sources: quest 5052 progress text (Agamaggan's body, the Downs as his maw)
quest 3523 description (Scourge deal in the Downs)

entries.title: The Mor'shan Rampart
body: A Horde fortification with a tall watch tower on the northern edge of the Barrens, where the road climbs into the forests of Ashenvale. It is the gateway of the Horde's campaign against the night elves.

Kadrak commands the tower and sends recruits on to the outposts at Splintertree and the Zoram Strand. He keeps a hard watch on the road and deals harshly with the Alliance runners who try to carry messages across the Barrens.
sources: quest 3921 (Mor'shan Rampart between the Barrens and Ashenvale)

entries.title: Thork
body: The orc who commands the Crossroads for the Warchief. He welcomes anyone who minds their own business and has no time for anyone who doesn't, and his main concern is the caravans from Durotar that keep his town fed and armed.

Thork thinks like a soldier: find the enemy's leader and cut it off. He sent warriors after the Razormane raider Kreenig Snarlsnout, and was astonished to learn that the true leaders of the raids were quilboars he had never heard of. He has less patience for grief: when the widowed Mankrik came asking for help, Thork told him his rage was clouding his judgement.

entries.title: Sergra Darkthorn
body: An orc shaman at the Crossroads who takes charge of new arrivals and teaches the hunt of the Barrens, from plainstriders and zhevra up to the prowlers and the great cat Echeyakee. Thrall believes she is something special. Kargal Battlescar at Far Watch is less sure.

Sergra demands respect and does not tolerate insolence. She is proud that Thrall has declared the Horde's women equal to its men. She is not without doubts, though: after sending hunters to defile the raptors' nests, she wondered aloud whether she had been too heavy-handed.

entries.title: Tonga Runetotem
body: A tauren druid sent from Thunder Bluff to find the source of the strange power seeping into the Barrens. He works from the Crossroads, sending helpers out to the oases to search their waters and test what they find.

Tonga is patient and quietly sad about the land. He believes in holding on to what is true and lasting in a changeable world, and he shares what he learns: samples of the oases' altered shells went to his clanmate Mura in Silverpine Forest, in the hope they might help heal that dying forest.

entries.title: Regthar Deathgate
body: An orc who holds the Horde's bunkers west of the Crossroads and leads the war against the Kolkar centaurs. The centaurs have hounded the tauren for years, but they used to be scattered; now new leaders have rallied them, and Regthar means to kill each one.

He collects their heads: Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish and finally the warlord Hezrul Bloodmark. The Kolkar answered by sending a war party from their homeland in Desolace under Warlord Krom'zar to attack his bunkers, and when it was defeated, Regthar made sure word reached Thrall.

entries.title: Mankrik
body: An orc warrior who stands at the edge of the Crossroads every day, watching the horizon for quilboars. He and his wife were caught by Bristlebacks at a small tauren camp in the south; she held off three of them alone before more arrived, and he was beaten down trying to draw them away.

A tauren druid found Mankrik on the Gold Road and tended his wounds. He came north to ask for help, found little, and now feeds his grief with hatred, killing every quilboar he meets. Her body was later found where the battle took place.

entries.title: Mangletooth
body: A Razormane quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo. His own tribe turned their backs on him and left him to rot, and he expects to die there, but he is not finished: he trades secrets and the magic of Agamaggan for help against his enemies.

Mangletooth hates the rival Bristleback tribe and the Razormane leaders who abandoned him in equal measure. It was he who revealed that the raids on the Crossroads were led by Nak, Kuz and Lok Orcbane, three Razormane who came out of Razorfen Kraul.
sources: quests 878, 5052, 879, 906 descriptions, progress and offer texts

entries.title: Gazlowe
body: The goblin boss of Ratchet, with a warehouse, an observatory waiting for its lens and a firm grip on the town's business. He pays well for good work and remembers who helped him.

Gazlowe takes losses personally. When the Southsea pirates began raiding his shipments and set up camp on his doorstep, he grumbled that the fleets the trade princes paid for were doing nothing, and hired adventurers to deal with the pirates himself.

entries.title: The Living Oases
body: For a long time the Barrens was a dry husk, scorched by ancient war. Then, within the past few years, oases began to form, and plants and animals clustered around them, growing in strange ways.

The druids of Thunder Bluff traced the power to fissures beneath the oases' waters, which could bring dead seeds to life, and found a taint in the shells of the turtles that swim in them. It felt to them as though the land were dreaming and could not wake.

The trail led to the Wailing Caverns, where the druid Naralex lies trapped in a nightmare of his own making. The water that brings life to the Barrens is the same water that carries his nightmare to the surface.

entries.title: Agamaggan, the Boar God
body: The quilboars tell of a battle of gods in the War of the Ancients, ten thousand years ago. Agamaggan, the great boar demigod, fell in that war, his blood raining onto the earth and his bones torn apart.

Where his blood touched the ground, giant thorns burst out of the soil. The quilboars gather wherever the thorns grow, and the greatest of these places is the Razorfen, which they believe is made of his body. Red stones laced with his blood are dug up there, and quilboar shamans draw his power from them for their magic.
Both the Razormane and the Bristleback revere Agamaggan, and both claim his strength for their war over the Barrens.
sources: creature 3430 Mangletooth gossip (Agamaggan fell in the War of the Ancients)
pre-Cataclysm lore: Agamaggan as a demigod

entries.title: The Horde Crosses the Barrens
body: When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor, their journey took them across the Barrens. It was a hard crossing through unknown country, and Thrall sent Grom Hellscream and his Warsong clan north into the forests of Ashenvale for timber, where they soon came to blows with the night elves. But on these plains the orcs also met Cairne Bloodhoof and his tauren, and won the friendship that brought the tauren into the Horde.

After the war, with Durotar settled, the Barrens became the land that bound the Horde together. The Crossroads guards the roads between orc and tauren country, the Mor'shan Rampart faces the night elves, and Thrall keeps watch over all of it: his officers send their reports to Orgrimmar, and a defeat of the Kolkar or the death of a Razormane chief soon reaches the Warchief's ears.
sources: page text 175758 (orcs crossed Kalimdor's Barrens, befriended Cairne, Hellscream in Ashenvale)
pre-Cataclysm lore: Warcraft III orc campaign

entries.title: Rexxar's Trail
body: In the years after the Horde settled Durotar, the half-ogre wanderer Rexxar, last of the mok'nathal, travelled the Barrens on Thrall's business. With him went the troll Rokhan and the pandaren brewmaster Chen Stormstout.

Their path left marks that are still found today. Rexxar killed a harpy called Bloodfeather, whose sister Serena led the Witchwing harpies against the Horde to avenge her. One of Chen's empty kegs still turns up on the plains, and a brewmaster in Ratchet keeps his recipes, handed down through his own teacher.
sources: quest 1060 offer text (Rokhan went with the mok'nathal)
quests 819, 821, 822 descriptions and offer texts (Chen traveled with Rexxar, recipe passed down)
pre-Cataclysm lore: Warcraft III The Frozen Throne, Rexxar's campaign

entries.title: The Great Beasts of the Plains
body: To the tauren hunters of the Barrens, certain beasts are more than prey. Each has a name in their tongue, Taurahe, and a hunter who defeats one is said to carry its spirit afterwards.

Echeyakee, Whitemist, is the king of the savannah cats, both mercy and death. Ishamuhale, Speartooth, is a raptor that kills simply because it is in its nature. The kodo Lakota'mani, Earthshaker, walks with steps like thunder; the thunder lizard Owatanka, Bluebolt, was struck by lightning long ago and never tires; and the thunderhawk Washte Pawne, Spirit Biter, teaches the pain of regret. Off the coast swims Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, a sea beast whom even the Theramore soldiers fear.
